mission_09: You have implemented counterfactual reasoning using the potential outcomes framework, the foundation of modern causal inference. The T-learner and S-learner are simple but effective meta-learners for estimating individual treatment effects. The fundamental problem demonstration makes clear why causal inference is challenging: for every unit, one potential outcome is forever unobserved. This is why we need assumptions (ignorability, overlap, SUTVA) and methods (randomization, matching, IV, RDD) to recover causal effects from incomplete data. Counterfactual prediction — estimating what would have happened under a different treatment — is the key to personalized decision-making. These techniques power recommendation systems, precision medicine, and targeted marketing by identifying which individuals will benefit most from an intervention.
